children: The consumer confidence indicator in Slovenia fell by 1 percentage point month-on-month to -23 in September 2026 from -22 in the previous month.
This marked the lowest reading in four months, as expectations regarding the economic situation for the past 12 months (-38 vs -37 in August) and the year ahead (-29 vs -27) worsened.
Households’ assessments of their financial situation over the past 12 months (-19 vs -16) also deteriorated, while those for the year ahead improved slightly (-14 vs -15).
Moreover, savings prospects over the next 12 months weakened (-14 vs -10).
In contrast, willingness to make major purchases over the next 12 months improved (-31 vs -32).
Among other indicators, price expectations for the past 12 months increased to 68 from 65, while those for the next 12 months rose to 61 from 56.
Concerns about unemployment a year ahead eased, falling to 17 from 22.

title: Slovenia Consumer Confidence Falls to 4-Month Low
